records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:84 — [advisory P2 confidence 75] `self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` leaves already-started workers running when a later `process.start()` raises during resource exhaustion, leaking Redis/Kafka workers from a constructor that never returns to its caller; the strongest rebuttal is that daemon children exit with the consumer, but that does not clean them up when strategy construction fails while the parent remains alive.
records.rationale: Looking at the _create_processes method (lines 78-81), it loops through process_to_shards_map and calls _create_process_for_shards for each process_index. The _create_process_for_shards method (lines 83-117) creates and starts a process, storing it in self.processes[process_index]. If an exception occurs during creation of a later process (e.g., process_index 2), the already-started processes (process_index 0 and 1) remain running with no cleanup.
